title: SLIDE uncovers a keratinocyte-centered signal in systemic sclerosis
summary: An interpretable machine-learning analysis of multi-omic systemic-sclerosis data identified an unexplored keratinocyte-centered signature, validated by protein staining, and a previously unreported interaction between myeloid-cell and fibroblast states and macrophage HLA signaling. The same study also analyzed CD4 T-cell clonal expansion, but this record treats the paper's disease-mechanism findings as one discovery.
ai_technology: SLIDE (Significant Latent Factor Interaction Discovery and Exploration)
organization: University of Pittsburgh and Cornell University

evidence.tested: An interpretable machine-learning analysis of multi-omic systemic-sclerosis data identified an unexplored keratinocyte-centered signature, validated by protein staining, and a previously unreported interaction between myeloid-cell and fibroblast states and macrophage HLA signaling.
evidence.unknown: The paper reports computationally identified relationships and validation of one signature by protein staining; these findings do not by themselves establish causal mechanisms or clinical utility.
evidence.ai_role: SLIDE integrated single-cell and spatial multi-omic data, identified interacting latent factors associated with systemic-sclerosis disease severity, and surfaced candidate mechanisms; the keratinocyte signal was checked with protein staining by the study team.
